Connecting a model training script to a managed distributed runtime.

Distributed training is a systems topic as much as a machine-learning topic: workers need a coherent strategy, and faster compute has to justify communication and startup costs.

The practical idea

A SageMaker walkthrough connecting distributed data-parallel training to hosted inference and cleanup.

The problem

Increasing instance count is not enough to make training distributed. The training script, runtime configuration, and data-parallel strategy must agree.

What the repository covers

The guide introduces SageMaker’s distributed data parallel library, role setup, the training script, TensorFlow estimator configuration, training, endpoint deployment, inference, and cleanup.

The tradeoff

A managed runtime removes some infrastructure setup while adding service-specific dependencies and cloud costs. With a small dataset like MNIST, startup and communication overhead may outweigh the benefit of another worker.

Evidence and limits

The repository is a learning walkthrough. It does not provide a measured scaling curve, cost-per-training-run comparison, or independently reproduced multi-node result. The portfolio presents it as exploration rather than a production training platform.

A stronger follow-up

Hold the target quality and dataset fixed, compare one worker with several, and report both wall-clock time and total compute cost. That reveals whether scaling improved the actual objective.

Design alternatives, compared

Architectural analysis of the choices described above. These comparisons do not reconstruct undocumented decision history.

Design choices, alternatives, and their tradeoffs
Choice exploredAlternativeWhat changes
Managed distributed data parallel setupA single-worker baselineAdds a scaling path, but communication and startup can dominate a small workload. A measured comparison is needed.
Hosted inference endpointKeep inference entirely in a notebookDemonstrates a deployment workflow, while introducing endpoint lifecycle and service-cost responsibilities.
Did another worker improve time to useful model quality, or just increase the bill?
